messages.author: 03290ff051991093
messages.subject: Dropping Record
parts:
How can I drop a record when writing a mapper (or reducer)?

For example, let's say I only want to keep a record if some condition is satisfied (e.g. x>8). So if for example x=4, do I just write
return(NULL)
or do I have to write something like
return(keyval(NA, NA))

Is there a recommended/standard way to do this?

Thanks!

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#730] Dropping Record
parts:
NULL or keyval(NULL, NULL) are equivalent. keyval(NA, NA) is a different thing. See also https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/Keyval-types-and-combinations


Antonio

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#730] Dropping Record
parts:
Antonio,

Thanks a lot for the link, it is very helpful.

So after trying various cases, I found out the following result:
  1. If I try use NULL keys, it does not work to selectively drop records, since I get the error message, "can't mix NULL and not NULL key keyval pairs."
  2. If I use 0-length keyval for the records I want to drop, I don't get an error message, but for the records I do want to keep, there is a problem. In particular, for the records I do want to keep, I use return(keyval(x, y)), where y is a 1 by 2 matrix. However, while rmr keeps the first column of that matrix, it drops the second column of that matrix, although I would like to keep that column. 
  3. The "normal case" does work, where I use return(keyval(NA, y)) for the records I want to discard, and return(keyval(x, y)) for the records I want to keep.
Again, thanks for pointing out that link. And I also would like to commend you for writing rmr. I'm really shocked how simple it is to write mapreduce jobs in rmr, and how the whole syntax is very R-like so that one often forgets that one is actually using Hadoop.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#732] Dropping Record
parts:
On Mon, Apr 29, 2013 at 1:17 AM, Michael Smith <my.r...@gmail.com> wrote:
Antonio,

Thanks a lot for the link, it is very helpful.

So after trying various cases, I found out the following result:
  1. If I try use NULL keys, it does not work to selectively drop records, since I get the error message, "can't mix NULL and not NULL key keyval pairs."

Doesn't happen to me, so we need to have some code here to make the discussion concrete.

from.dfs(mapreduce(to.dfs(1:10), map = function(k,v) if(sum(v) < 15) keyval(1,v), reduce = function(k,vv) sum(vv)))

Of course this would go though in a single map call at defaults or any reasonable setting, so I set

rmr.options(keyval.length=2)

beforehand. That makes rmr call the map function twice on this example. The second time the map function returns NULL. It works just fine. What you may be doing is mixing keyval(1,10) and keyval(NULL, 10). That is something I decided to disallow when it tightened the semantics for keyval related operations following some bug reports and requests for clarfication. The idea is that you need to be able to do recycling of keyval args to bring them to the same lenght (or nrow if matrix or data frame). When you have 0-length and non-0-length there is no amount of recycling that will achieve that. An exception is cut for to.dfs or map only job. When all the keys are NULL it is understood as keys missing. If there is a reduce phase, we need keys to guide the grouping, so this is disallowed. If there is a mix of keyval pairs, some with keys and some without, even without reduce, I couldn't come up with any meaningful definition that was consistent with the rest, but it may be just me. Imagine that keyval is just a cbind with a special role for some columns and that when you call map multiple times you need to apply a rbind to keys and values, after recycling of arguments, to make them into a single data structure (that doesn't always happen, but the idea is that it should always be possible, either in the preparation to the reduce call or in a from.dfs call). If you call cbind (NULL, mtcars) it fails but let's say we relaxed it to return mtcars;  then you call cbind(1, mtcars) and it will add a column if 1s. Then you try to rbind them and it will fail because of the discrepancy in the number of columns. We could switch to a semantics inspired by rbind.fill and see where that leads us (match same name cols, add all the other cols, fill in with NAs. In fact, we are already using rbind.fill behind the scenes to support outer joins.

1. If I use 0-length keyval for the records I want to drop, I don't get an error message, but for the records I do want to keep, there is a problem. In particular, for the records I do want to keep, I use return(keyval(x, y)), where y is a 1 by 2 matrix. However, while rmr keeps the first column of that matrix, it drops the second column of that matrix, although I would like to keep that column.
That's a bug and needs to be fixed, please provide a test case.
1. The "normal case" does work, where I use return(keyval(NA, y)) for the records I want to discard, and return(keyval(x, y)) for the records I want to keep.
That is not filtering, you can do it, but it doesn't discard any records unless you later check for NA and discard them. I would call it a workaround at best.

Again, thanks for pointing out that link. And I also would like to commend you for writing rmr. I'm really shocked how simple it is to write mapreduce jobs in rmr, and how the whole syntax is very R-like so that one often forgets that one is actually using Hadoop.

Thanks a lot, but there is still so much more work to do! 


Antonio

On Monday, April 29, 2013 1:37:14 PM UTC+8, Antonio Piccolboni wrote:
NULL or keyval(NULL, NULL) are equivalent. keyval(NA, NA) is a different thing. See also https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/Keyval-types-and-combinations


Antonio

parts:
So after trying various cases, I found out the following result:
  1. If I try use NULL keys, it does not work to selectively drop records, since I get the error message, "can't mix NULL and not NULL key keyval pairs."

What you may be doing is mixing keyval(1,10) and keyval(NULL, 10). That is something I decided to disallow when it tightened the semantics for keyval related operations following some bug reports and requests for clarfication.

Yes, keyval(NULL, 10) is what I meant by 'NULL keys', the way I understand the first table in your link, since it is key=NULL and value=(length>0). By the way, I'm fine with this design choice, I just wanted to report what worked and what didn't work for me when trying to drop some records.

1. If I use 0-length keyval for the records I want to drop, I don't get an error message, but for the records I do want to keep, there is a problem. In particular, for the records I do want to keep, I use return(keyval(x, y)), where y is a 1 by 2 matrix. However, while rmr keeps the first column of that matrix, it drops the second column of that matrix, although I would like to keep that column. 
That's a bug and needs to be fixed, please provide a test case.

Strange, today I cannot reproduce this any more. If I use return(NULL) (which is according to my understanding does the same as return(keyval(NULL, NULL))), the record gets dropped and the for the records I want to keep, the second column of the matrix is not discarded. So this works fine, and according to my understanding this is the preferred method of selectively dropping records. In case I will later encounter this strange behavior again, I'll let you know.

1. The "normal case" does work, where I use return(keyval(NA, y)) for the records I want to discard, and return(keyval(x, y)) for the records I want to keep.
That is not filtering, you can do it, but it doesn't discard any records unless you later check for NA and discard them. I would call it a workaround at best.

Actually, the NAs do get dropped when I run the following code, and I don't have to remove the NAs later:

library("rmr2")
rmr.options(backend = "local")
rmr.options(keyval.length = 2)
mapper <- function(k, v) {
  if(sum(v) < 15) {                     # Return 'normal case'.
    return(keyval(1, v))
  } else {                              # Return 'NA key'.
    return(keyval(NA, v))
  }
}
output <- mapreduce(to.dfs(keyval(1:10)), map = mapper)
from.dfs(output)

I do agree though that it would be better to use your example from your previous post, which returns NULL in case we don't want to keep the record.

messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#734] Dropping Record
parts:
This happens because keys are used for grouping. Grouping is done with split and split drops NA's (undocumented)
```
> split(2:3, c(1, NA))
$`1`
[1] 2
```
I've already overridden split's behavior in a couple of cases, but there's a performance penalty to pay.  Do you think split should just treat NA as another value? The problem is that NA == NA is not true, is NA, so one has to special case the NAs.


Antonio

I think the non-reproducible behavior about the NULL values was because earlier I was still using the master branch that dealt with issue #26. With version 2.2.0 the problem is gone.

About the NAs, I do not have a strong opinion. Currently I don't see a reason why the NAs should be kept by split. So the current way rmr handles this (i.e. dropping the NAs) is fine with me. Overriding split's behavior is probably not worth the performance penalty you have to pay (not even speaking about making the code more complicated to maintain and extend).

Nonetheless, in case I later come across a compelling reason why the NAs should be kept, I'll let you know.
